questions.q: What are the three phases of rising strong, in order?
a: Reckoning, rumbling, revolution
Reflection, repair, renewal
Notice, negotiate, normalize
Recover, rebuild, repeat
questions.why: The overview names the phases as reckoning with emotions, rumbling with stories, and revolutionizing your attitude.

a: Recognizing your emotions and asking why you feel them
Ignoring your feelings until they fade
Writing a plan for avoiding failure
Asking others to explain your behavior
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes reckoning as giving yourself permission to feel, then getting curious about the reason.

questions.q: What is the shitty first draft in the summary?
a: The story you write down about what you are feeling
The first version of a book manuscript
A list of your biggest past mistakes
A letter apologizing to someone you hurt
questions.why: Lesson 2 has you fill in blanks about your emotions, body, thinking and actions to capture the story you are telling yourself.

questions.q: How does rumbling help with the stories we tell ourselves?
a: It gives distance so you can judge whether the story is true
It replaces bad stories with more comforting ones
It stops you from feeling emotions altogether
It proves that your first instincts are correct
questions.why: Lesson 2 compares rumbling to a lie detector for your thoughts, letting you assess the story instead of believing it.

questions.q: What did Brené learn from her revolution about homelessness?
a: Asking for help is part of rising strong, not weakness
She should avoid homeless people entirely
Generosity only means giving money
Guilt is the best motivator for change
questions.why: Lesson 3 says she realized that asking for help is a key part of rising strong rather than a sign of weakness.
